highlights.title: [$] The "rnull" Rust block driver
highlights.summary: In June 2026 a patch set added a Rust implementation of the null block driver (rnull) that matches the feature set of the existing C version.
highlights.detail: The rnull driver is used for benchmarking block‑layer performance by instantly completing requests. The Rust version demonstrates that simple kernel drivers can now be written with the kernel's Rust APIs, enabling direct C vs Rust performance comparisons.

highlights.title: I accidentally turned LLM memory into program analysis
highlights.summary: A developer discovered that the internal memory of a large language model can be repurposed to perform program analysis tasks.
highlights.detail: The technique treats the model's attention and hidden states as a searchable index of code patterns, enabling static‑like analysis without external tooling. It highlights a novel, low‑cost way to leverage existing LLMs for software inspection.

highlights.title: Car: Dolphin 26.08 and KIO performance improvements
highlights.summary: Dolphin 26.08’s file‑manager improvements make copying many small files more than twice as fast as in April.
highlights.detail: The speed gain comes from reduced per‑file overhead; as file size grows, the benefit diminishes because I/O dominates. KIO still trails the traditional cp command, though ongoing batching work aims to close the remaining gap.

highlights.title: abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus
highlights.summary: GitNexus is a zero‑server, browser‑based code intelligence engine that builds interactive knowledge graphs from any Git repository.
highlights.detail: It runs entirely client‑side, supports repositories from GitHub, GitLab, Azure, or local ZIP files, and includes a Graph RAG agent to answer code‑related queries without backend infrastructure.

highlights.title: abi/screenshot-to-code
highlights.summary: screenshot‑to‑code converts UI screenshots into clean HTML, Tailwind, React, or Vue code.
highlights.detail: The tool parses visual elements from an image and generates corresponding markup, streamlining the workflow from design mockup to production‑ready front‑end code across multiple frameworks.

items.summary: Tencent's Hy4-preview text‑generation model has been downloaded 1,394 times and received 258 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is listed under the text‑generation category and is a preview release, indicating early‑stage availability for experimentation. Its modest download count suggests niche interest compared to larger community models.

items.title: Model: unsloth/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF
items.summary: unsloth's GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF model has attracted 27,288 downloads and 254 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: This GGUF‑formatted variant is optimized for flash storage and fast inference, targeting users who need a lightweight yet capable text‑generation model. The high download volume reflects strong community demand for efficient deployments.

items.title: Model: zai-org/GLM-5.3
items.summary: zai‑org's GLM-5.3 model recorded 8,804 downloads and 1,192 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: Despite fewer downloads than some peers, the model’s like‑to‑download ratio is high, indicating that users who try it find it valuable. It is also listed under the text‑generation category.

items.title: 3D Printed Piano Action Faithful to the Original
items.summary: A 3D‑printed piano action faithfully reproduces the original mechanism’s velocity and control characteristics.
items.detail: The printed components capture the intricate linkages and timing required for expressive playing, offering a low‑cost alternative to machining or sourcing vintage parts while preserving tactile fidelity.

items.title: Casting Engine Parts from 3D Prints
items.summary: 3D‑printed patterns are used to cast metal engine parts, reducing material waste compared to traditional billet milling.
items.detail: The approach leverages additive manufacturing to create molds, allowing multiple castings from a single print and minimizing the scrap generated by subtractive machining processes.

items.title: DOOM Played on Series of 555 Timers
items.summary: A full version of DOOM has been recreated using a chain of 555 timer circuits.
items.detail: The project demonstrates that any software can, in principle, be implemented in pure hardware, though the complexity and component count make it impractical for modern applications. It serves as a proof‑of‑concept for hardware‑only computing.

items.title: Hackaday Podcast Episode 384: OCR MOD Records, Magical PCBs, and the Gravity of Space Stations
items.summary: Hackaday Podcast Episode 384 covers OCR MOD records, innovative PCBs, and experiments on space‑station gravity.
items.detail: The episode highlights recent Hackaday articles, discussing advances in optical character recognition, novel printed‑circuit‑board designs, and the challenges of conducting experiments in microgravity environments.

items.title: ajeetdsouza/zoxide
items.summary: zoxide is a smarter cd command that supports all major shells.
items.detail: Implemented in Rust, it replaces the default cd behavior and learns directory usage patterns to prioritize frequently visited paths, offering faster navigation across Bash, Zsh, Fish, and other common shells.

items.title: anthropics/claude-plugins-official
items.summary: Claude-plugins-official is Anthropic's curated directory of high‑quality Claude code plugins.
items.detail: The repository aggregates community‑contributed plugins that extend Claude's functionality, with Anthropic overseeing quality and compatibility, making it easier for developers to discover and integrate ready‑made extensions.

items.title: apache/datafusion
items.summary: Apache DataFusion is an open‑source SQL query engine written in Rust.
items.detail: Part of the Apache Arrow ecosystem, DataFusion executes ANSI‑SQL queries on in‑memory data, can be embedded in applications, and serves as a foundation for building analytical workloads.

items.title: apache/opendal
items.summary: Apache OpenDAL provides a unified abstraction layer for accessing multiple storage services.
items.detail: The library offers a single API to interact with diverse backends such as S3, Azure Blob, and Google Cloud Storage, simplifying code that needs to work across heterogeneous storage environments.
